title: Minimize the Total Price of the Trips
summary: Given a tree with n nodes and their associated prices, you can halve the prices of some non-adjacent nodes before performing trips.
statement: Given a tree with n nodes and their associated prices, you can halve the prices of some non-adjacent nodes before performing trips. Each trip starts from one node and ends at another, and the goal is to minimize the total price sum of all trips. You can choose which nodes to halve to achieve the minimum total price.
constraints: edges describes a tree with even positive price per node.
Before all trips, you may halve prices at any set of pairwise nonadjacent nodes.
Each trip pays every node on its unique endpoint-inclusive path; return the minimum total across all trips.
hints: First count how often each node appears across the unique trip paths.
Tree DP returns two costs per subtree: current node full-price or halved.
A full-price node allows either child state; a halved node forces every child to full price.
The two states enumerate every independent set of halved nodes, and visit counts make each state cost equal to all trip payments.
editorial: The two states enumerate every independent set of halved nodes, and visit counts make each state cost equal to all trip payments.
